steps.text: Grease and flour two 8x4-inch loaf pans.
Sift flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together in a large bowl; make a well in the center.

Whisk eggs, butter, sugar, and vanilla extract together in a separate bowl; fold in mango, coconut, and walnuts. Pour this mixture into the well in flour mixture; stir to combine. Pour batter into prepared loaf pans; let sit at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 1 hour. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes before removing to cool completely on a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Mango Bread
raw_recipe.description: This moist mango bread is easy to make with chopped fresh mango, shredded coconut, walnuts and easy baking ingredients for a delicious tropical treat!

review.reviewBody: very easy to make, and so tasty! I don't have regular bread pans, just a set of four small ones, so I used those, and mini muffin tins. Also switched out the walnuts for pecans, and everything still worked out great!

I substituted Bob’s Redmill 1 to 1 gluten free flour in this recipe and it turned out great! I wasn’t sure which size loaf pans to use, but after mixing up the batter decided that three 5x3 pans would be perfect. I greased the pans but didn’t bother flouring them and the bread slipped right out. 45 minutes was definitely enough! So good- my child with celiac disease loves this sweet treat!

A friend called this the best mango bread she has ever eaten. I was pleasantly surprised at how well this turned out. There are walnut haters in my household so I left the nuts out. The honey mango and coconut alone tasted great. I made these into mango muffins and cooked for about 25 minutes at altitude. Another friend asked me to make this again soon and I just might.

This came out great. I did change a bit as I always do. I had no shredded coconut but I did have coconut milk. That worked. I always put in less sugar as most breads are too sweet, so I used 1/4 cup of organic cane juice crystals and 1/8 cup of organic blue agave.And I finely chopped pecans instead of big pieces of walnuts. I prefer it that way. Its perfect. Oh.. and I decided on muffins that take about 20 minutes to bake instead of a bread. I love it!

This came out so light and fluffy! I used Hayden mango and cut it into half inch chunks. They held up nicely throughout. I also didn’t have a loaf pan so I used a 9x13 cake pan and baked for 45 minutes. It’s golden and gorgeous.
Loved it added more coconut and nuts and let the mango sit to create juice just to give it a better mango flavor. It’s delicious
This is delicious! I used just two cups of mango and added one cup of very ripe mashed bananas, a bit extra cinnamon and vanilla. It is the perfect tropical fruit bread.

This recipe is wonderful! I only made one change, which was to cut the sugar in half, because my mangoes were VERY ripe and sweet. I made 1 loaf and 6 muffins. The muffins cooked in 25 minutes and were nice and soft. The loaf is the main event, though - a perfect quick bread!

It's mango time in Florida and it's great to get them right off the trees! I get so many sometimes and this was a perfect use for them. The coconut is a real compliment & bread was moist and delishous. I had to use sliced (toasted) almonds - all I had in the pantry. I will try some macadamia's next time as I will certainly make again. Also, 350 on convection bake in my oven, both loaves made in same pans were ready in 35 min. and I reduced the sugar by 1/4 c.
Yes I made it. I blended the mangoes. I didn’t have shredded coconut or walnuts so I used extra mangoes. Also added diced mangoes on top. It was a hit!! Nice and moist.
Turned out great. Moist and flavorful. Substituted two cups (296 grams) Bob’s Red Mill Gluten-free 1 to 1 baking flour.

I kept a few quart size bags of chopped mangoes that I picked last summer. I measured 2 cups of mangoes before freezing it. Just thawed it and drained the excess liquids before adding to the recipe. My husband likes the coconut flakes and walnuts that added depth to this recipe. I totally agree. My friend that are fortunate enough to have a mango tree extend to their yard is such a blessing here on the island. I shared a few loaves with her family and just loved it.
Excellent. Husband allergic to walnuts; substituted with Smokehouse almonds. Also, added candied ginger, dash of nutmeg, and a splash of coconut chocolate cream liqueur.
Every year I have tons of mangos from my tree and there's really not many good recipes for baked good. This is a good one!
Fantastic what a nice change!
I used brown sugar. Didn't have walnuts, ground up a few almonds and dropped in. The bread was extremely delicious. Love the chunks of mango in each bite.
Didn't taste much like mango.

My family loved his bread. I’ve made it multiple times. The second time used extra large eggs and I doubled the coconut and it was perfect. I also melted the butter and then let it cool. The flavor depends on the quality of the mangoes.

Yum! Our neighbor keeps giving us mangoes, so I keep making this bread! I doubled it, and used 1 1/3 cup brown sugar, 1 cup white sugar, and I added two bananas to it. Maybe next time I'll only add 3/4 cup white sugar; it was pretty sweet! Very delicious!
This was so moist and tasty. I used one 8x4x2 pan and two small ones, the small ones got done 10 minutes sooner than the larger pan. I followed the re pie as is.
